source.title: Spectral Probe-Circuits: A Three-Step Recipe for Identifying Attention-Head Circuits in Pretrained Transformers

page_placements.theme: Induction circuit composition in pretrained full transformers (upstream previous-token, duplicate-token and context heads)

record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction-pattern selectivity and tests candidate circuits with head ablations and matched-random controls, a conceptual test using a different identification procedure from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on synthetic induction and natural-text induction, including selectivity measurements and causal ablations. It also reports a training-onset estimate for induction heads. The TS-51M key-retrieval probe was deliberately injected during training and is not treated as evidence for naturally occurring induction. The text cites the original phase-transition finding but does not report its own induction-related in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measure or a loss-curve bump.
record.test_reason: The study identifies induction heads in pretrained GPT-2-style, Pythia, OLMo and OLMoE models with its own selectivity screen. It confirms them by group ablation against matched-random controls, and it reports emergence timing and a data-shift test. This is a different method aimed at whether induction heads exist and matter across models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that a 3–6 head induction circuit (3–11 depending on threshold) is causally necessary in every model, sublinear in head count. Previous-token ablation confirms the compositional dependency. About 17–19% of heads do specialised work within the Pythia/GPT-2 family, though this does not hold across architectures. Induction-circuit granularity differs by model.
record.recipe_differences: Uses time-integrated participation ratio, an all-head task-pattern selectivity screen, and group ablation with matched-random and upper-bound controls. The study describes this as replacing the original sources' attribution-style identification workflow.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit size and ablation effect vary by model and selectivity threshold. The paper reports threshold-specific circuit sizes, a weaker matched-random differential in OLMoE, position-dependent class labels in Karpathy 124M, and stable circuit identity under the tested FineWeb-to-OWT shift.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating 8–9 previous-token heads (≥100×) eliminates synthetic induction in Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B and OLMoE 1B-7B. Matched-random controls leave it intact in Pythia and OLMo but not in OLMoE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pretrained full transformers up to 1B-active parameters, induction behaviour causally depends on upstream previous-token heads (V1's composition, beyond attention-only models).

record.code_released: https://github.com/ (the text names the repository as skydancerosel/spectral-probe-circuits)
record.problems: Most natural-text models are single pretrained checkpoints; the cross-seed experiment is on an intentionally trained key-retrieval probe rather than natural induction. The data-shift test is one short continuation between similar English web-text corpora. The timing result does not measure the ICL loss-by-token-index gain or loss-curve bump in V2. Some matched-random conditions are reported at one seed; the appendix reports substantial seed variance for the Pythia 1B matched-random case.
record.rows_left_out: No additional induction-ablation results omitted. The TS-51M probe-task ablation and cross-seed results were not entered as induction rows because the task was deliberately injected key retrieval rather than naturally occurring repeated-token induction. BOS-fraction and other non-induction results were also excluded.

untested.parts: No small attention-only transformers are studied. Composition with previous-token heads is shown only in full 1B-class LMs (see fits_no_version). QK/OV composition is not traced.
Concurrent in-context-learning gain (loss vs token index) and loss-curve bump not measured. Abruptness is shown only via a PR crossing window in one model.
Entire version: no in-context-learning (loss by token index) measure.
Training seeds of natural-text models, other architectures (non-transformer) and modalities. The TS-51M seeds use an injected key-retrieval task.
Effect of data properties on whether or when induction heads form, or on in-context learning. Only persistence under a similar-corpus continuation is tested.
Entire version: sub-steps of formation are not analysed.

missing.what: Training fraction at which induction selectivity crosses 50× in Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B and OLMoE: about 0.3–2.1% of training. The spectral signal precedes formation.
Matched-random seed sensitivity: Pythia 1B seed-123 control gives 36.05% vs 8-seed mean 8.02% (std 8.2pp); OLMoE std 3.49pp.
Pythia 410M L11H14, primarily a first-token head with 124× induction, halves induction on its own when ablated.

record.verdict_notes: V1 names small attention-only transformers, which this study does not use, so V1 links were dropped and the composition evidence went to fits_no_version. The TS-51M key-retrieval task is deliberately injected and its circuit sits in L0, so it is excluded. The paper is a methods paper. The study's own spectral-pick rows (R1, R11) mix method performance with induction evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests induction-pattern attention, induction-task ablations, and the effect of ablating previous-token heads on induction. It does not directly trace the full QK/OV composition of the classic previous-token-plus-induction circuit in every model.
It reports the onset window for induction-class selectivity in Karpathy 124M, but does not measure the specified loss bump or the loss-falling-with-token-index in-context-learning gain at that time.
No large-transformer measure of most in-context learning, defined as loss falling with token index, is reported.

The natural-text induction panel covers the reported model configurations, but not all model families, modalities, or architectures. The TS-51M seed-specific results concern an intentionally trained key-retrieval probe, not natural induction.

The data-shift test is a short continuation from FineWeb to similar English web text (OWT) on one already-trained model. Other training-data shifts and their effects on induction formation or in-context learning are not tested.
The study does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or measure which mechanism carries few-shot task learning.
It does not test whether induction-head formation itself consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.
